name: code_read_file

input.body:
label: bug
file: src/notifications/templates.ts

The password reset (and other) emails build links from `BASE_URL`, which falls back to `http://localhost:3000` whenever the `PUBLIC_URL` environment variable isn't set (templates.ts line 8). It looks like last week's release stopped setting `PUBLIC_URL` in production, so emails silently fall back to localhost instead of the real public URL. Fix by ensuring `PUBLIC_URL` is always configured in the production environment, and consider making `templates.ts` fail loudly (throw or log an error) instead of silently defaulting to localhost when it's missing.

input.title: Fix password reset email linking to localhost in production
input.body:
File: src/notifications/templates.ts

BASE_URL falls back to "http://localhost:3000" whenever process.env.PUBLIC_URL is not set, and this value is used to build the password reset link (and other links) sent in emails. In production, PUBLIC_URL is apparently not being set, so users receive reset links pointing at localhost instead of the real site.

Proposed fix: ensure PUBLIC_URL is required/validated at startup (e.g. via config validation) so the app fails fast or logs clearly if it's missing in production, rather than silently falling back to localhost. Alternatively, derive BASE_URL from a dedicated, environment-specific config value (e.g. config.publicUrl) that is guaranteed to be set correctly per deployment environment, and remove the localhost fallback for non-development environments. This will ensure passwordResetEmail, rollupText, and scheduledExportEmail all generate correct links in production.
